title: What can waves tell us?
target: Distinguish a signal’s travel from the motion of its source.
criteria: Identify what a wave can carry.
Separate signal travel time from source speed.
Name evidence needed to interpret an observation.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A floating marker bobs as a small water wave passes. What can travel onward even though the marker stays near its location?
options: Only the marker’s mass, with no energy.
All the marker’s matter must travel with the crest.
Nothing, because waves cannot move.
Energy carried by the wave.
cpa.guide: In the simple wave model, energy propagates while material oscillates locally.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A rope pulse reaches a hanging bell and moves it. Which observation supports energy transfer?
options: The rope must be flowing continuously into the bell.
The bell begins moving after the pulse arrives.
The entire rope becomes part of the bell.
The pulse creates matter.
cpa.guide: Work on the bell demonstrates transferred energy; bulk rope transport is unnecessary.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A signal travels 84 m from a stationary source at 28 m/s. What is one-way travel time?
cpa.guide: t = d/v = 84/28 = 3.0 s. Signal speed does not imply source motion.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A stationary lighthouse sends a flash. The flash travels away rapidly. What can be inferred about the lighthouse’s own speed from signal speed alone?
options: Nothing definite; signal propagation and source motion are different.
It must accelerate with the flash.
It must move toward the observer.
It must move at the speed of light.
cpa.guide: A source can remain still while its signal propagates.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: To infer distance from a measured one-way signal delay, what additional information is essential?
options: Signal speed along the path.
Only the observer’s favorite unit.
Only the source’s color.
Only the receiver’s mass.
cpa.guide: Distance equals propagation speed times travel time in the constant-speed model.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A receiver detects a later pulse than expected. Which evidence would help distinguish a farther source from a slower propagation path?
options: An assumption that later always means faster.
Only the pulse arrival time again.
The receiver’s label.
Independent information about the path’s signal speed or the source distance.
cpa.guide: Travel time depends on both distance and speed; one delay cannot uniquely determine both.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
